title: Hunt component diagram
description: File-level component diagram of a Hunt session's changes: one node per file, edges are dependencies between files. Rendered by the Hunt client from `.hunt/graph.json`.

path.description: Worktree-relative path of a project file; identifies the node and is referenced by edges. Never a path under `node_modules`: installed packages are not part of the diagram.

review.description: How much a human should review this file, weighing its relevance (how often it is reused, architectural significance, weight for the business logic) together with how drastic its change is: 4 when an interface, data model, business rule, security-related or central abstraction changes substantially; 3 for a relevant file with a small change or an ordinary file with a substantial one; 2 for ordinary feature code with a contained change; 1 for leaf files, tests, styling, translations, boilerplate and mechanical edits. Required on every changed file, absent on an unchanged context file. Shown as a signal-strength icon on the node.

reviewReason.description: One sentence naming the deciding criteria behind `review`, e.g. `Changes the response type every client parses.`; shown when the icon is hovered.

source.description: `path` of the dependent file, e.g. the one that imports.

target.description: `path` of the file it depends on.

label.description: How `source` uses `target` in one to three words, so a reviewer understands the dependency without opening either file: a verb, a noun or both, e.g. `calls`, `validates input`, `maps rows`, `uses types`, `stores orders`, `test data`; never the name of the imported symbol or file (`PaginatedResult`, `user.service` are dropped).

description.description: Two to four sentences: how `source` uses `target` (which functions, types or data it takes and where in the flow) and what that use achieves for the change. Shown when the edge or one of its files is hovered.
